lessons.title: Data, Populations, Samples, and Bias
lessons.summary: Design reliable statistical investigations by defining populations, variables, samples, and defensible sampling methods.
outcomes: Distinguish a population, census, sample, parameter, and statistic in context.
Classify variables as categorical or numerical, and numerical data as discrete or continuous.
Apply simple random, systematic, stratified, quota, and convenience sampling appropriately.
Identify sources of bias and evaluate whether a statistical conclusion is trustworthy.

lessons.title: Measures of Centre, Spread, and Outliers
lessons.summary: Summarize and compare distributions using centre, spread, quartiles, standard deviation, box plots, and outlier criteria.
outcomes: Calculate and interpret mean, median, and mode.
Determine quartiles, range, and interquartile range using ordered data.
Calculate and interpret variance and standard deviation with technology.
Use box plots and the 1.5-IQR rule to compare distributions and identify outliers.

lessons.title: Frequency Tables, Grouped Data, and Cumulative Frequency
lessons.summary: Organize large data sets using frequencies, grouped intervals, histograms, cumulative frequency, and technology-based estimates.
outcomes: Construct and interpret frequency and cumulative frequency tables.
Use midpoints to estimate the mean and standard deviation of grouped data.
Draw and interpret histograms, including unequal class widths when frequency density is required.
Estimate medians, quartiles, and percentiles from cumulative frequency information.

lessons.title: Correlation, Regression, and Interpretation
lessons.summary: Analyse bivariate data using scatter plots, Pearson and Spearman coefficients, regression models, residuals, and contextual judgment.
outcomes: Describe scatter plots by form, direction, strength, and unusual features.
Calculate and interpret Pearson’s product-moment and Spearman’s rank correlation coefficients.
Find and interpret least-squares regression equations and predictions.
Evaluate interpolation, extrapolation, residuals, outliers, and the difference between association and causation.

lessons.title: Sets, Venn Diagrams, and Probability Language
lessons.summary: Use precise set notation and Venn diagrams to describe events, complements, unions, intersections, and structured counting.
outcomes: Use universal set, subset, complement, union, and intersection notation.
Translate verbal event descriptions into set notation and shaded regions.
Complete two-set and three-set Venn diagrams from counts or probabilities.
Apply complements and De Morgan’s laws to simplify event descriptions.

lessons.title: Probability Rules and Two-Way Tables
lessons.summary: Calculate event probabilities using complements, addition rules, equally likely outcomes, relative frequency, and two-way tables.
outcomes: Use the probability scale, complements, and equally likely sample spaces.
Apply the general addition rule and identify mutually exclusive events.
Calculate probabilities from frequencies, relative frequencies, and two-way tables.
Interpret probability answers in context and check whether they are reasonable.

lessons.title: Conditional Probability and Independent Events
lessons.summary: Use conditional probability, multiplication rules, and equivalent independence tests while distinguishing independence from mutual exclusivity.
outcomes: Calculate and interpret conditional probability.
Use the multiplication rule to find intersections.
Test whether events are independent using equivalent probability conditions.
Distinguish independent events from mutually exclusive events.

lessons.title: Tree Diagrams, Bayes, and Sequential Events
lessons.summary: Model multi-stage probability with trees, replacement rules, total probability, and reverse conditional reasoning.
outcomes: Construct tree diagrams with valid branch probabilities.
Multiply probabilities along paths and add disjoint terminal paths.
Model sampling with and without replacement.
Use total probability and Bayes-style reasoning to calculate reverse conditional probabilities.

lessons.title: Discrete Random Variables and Expected Value
lessons.summary: Construct discrete probability distributions, calculate event probabilities and expected values, and evaluate long-run decisions and fair games.
outcomes: Define a discrete random variable and validate its probability distribution.
Calculate probabilities of events from a distribution table.
Find and interpret expected value, mode, median, and quartiles for discrete distributions.
Use expected value to evaluate games and long-run decisions.

lessons.title: Binomial Distribution and Repeated Trials
lessons.summary: Recognize binomial settings, calculate exact and cumulative probabilities, and interpret the distribution’s mean, variance, and assumptions.
outcomes: Verify the conditions for a binomial model.
Calculate exact, at-most, at-least, and interval probabilities.
Find and interpret the mean, variance, and standard deviation of a binomial distribution.
Evaluate assumptions and distinguish binomial counts from other repeated-trial questions.

lessons.title: Normal Distribution, Probabilities, and Quantiles
lessons.summary: Use the normal model to calculate areas, inverse quantiles, standardized positions, expected counts, and contextual probabilities.
outcomes: Interpret \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\) in a normal model.
Calculate lower-tail, upper-tail, and interval probabilities.
Find quantiles and symmetric intervals using inverse normal calculations.
Apply normal probabilities to expected counts, repeated selections, and conditional contexts.

lessons.title: Inferential Statistics, Hypotheses, and Significance
lessons.summary: Move from sample evidence to population conclusions using null and alternative hypotheses, significance levels, p-values, and disciplined decision language.
outcomes: Distinguish population parameters from sample statistics in inference.
State appropriate null and alternative hypotheses.
Interpret significance level and p-value conceptually.
Make and communicate decisions using reject/do-not-reject language.

lessons.title: Two-Sample t-Tests for Comparing Means
lessons.summary: Compare two population means with pooled two-sample t-tests, one- and two-tailed alternatives, GDC output, and contextual conclusions.
outcomes: Recognize when a pooled two-sample t-test is appropriate and state its assumptions.
Form one-tailed and two-tailed hypotheses for two means.
Use GDC output to make decisions at stated significance levels.
Write precise contextual conclusions without overstating non-significant results.

lessons.title: Chi-Square Test for Independence
lessons.summary: Test whether two categorical variables are independent using observed and expected frequencies, degrees of freedom, GDC output, and validity checks.
outcomes: State hypotheses for a chi-square test of independence.
Calculate expected frequencies and degrees of freedom.
Use a GDC to obtain the chi-square statistic and p-value.
Check expected-frequency conditions, merge categories when required, and interpret the conclusion.

lessons.title: Chi-Square Goodness-of-Fit Test
lessons.summary: Compare observed categorical frequencies with a claimed distribution, calculate expected counts, check conditions, and interpret goodness-of-fit evidence.
outcomes: State hypotheses for a chi-square goodness-of-fit test.
Calculate expected frequencies from stated category probabilities.
Use \(df=k-1\), GDC output, and p-values to make a decision.
Merge low-expected-frequency categories appropriately and test discrete, binomial, or specified normal models.
